topic: Station rules: antennas, beacons, transmissions, repeaters, third parties, automatic control (G1B, G1E; 22 pool questions)

questions.question: What is the maximum height above ground for an antenna structure not near a public use airport without requiring notification to the FAA and registration with the FCC?

choices.A: 50 feet
choices.B: 100 feet
choices.C: 200 feet

questions.answer: 200 feet

questions.question: With which of the following conditions must beacon stations comply?

choices.A: No more than one beacon station may transmit in the same band from the same station location
choices.B: The frequency must be coordinated with the National Beacon Organization
choices.C: The frequency must be posted on the internet or published in a national periodical

questions.answer: No more than one beacon station may transmit in the same band from the same station location

questions.question: Which of the following is a purpose of a beacon station as identified in the FCC rules?

choices.A: Observation of propagation and reception
choices.B: Automatic identification of repeaters
choices.C: Transmission of bulletins of general interest to amateur radio licensees

questions.answer: Observation of propagation and reception

questions.question: Which of the following transmissions is permitted for all amateur stations?

choices.A: Unidentified transmissions of less than 10 seconds duration for test purposes only
choices.B: Automatic retransmission of other amateur signals by any amateur station
choices.C: Occasional retransmission of weather and propagation forecast information from US government stations
choices.D: Encrypted messages, if not intended to facilitate a criminal act

questions.answer: Occasional retransmission of weather and propagation forecast information from US government stations

questions.question: Which of the following one-way transmissions are permitted?

choices.A: Unidentified test transmissions of less than 10 seconds in duration
choices.B: Transmissions to assist with learning the International Morse code
choices.C: Regular transmissions offering equipment for sale, if intended for amateur radio use

questions.answer: Transmissions to assist with learning the International Morse code

questions.question: Under what conditions are state and local governments permitted to regulate amateur radio antenna structures?

choices.A: Under no circumstances, FCC rules take priority
choices.B: At any time and to any extent necessary to accomplish a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity, provided that proper filings are made with the FCC
choices.C: Only when such structures exceed 50 feet in height and are clearly visible 1,000 feet from the structure
choices.D: Amateur Service communications must be reasonably accommodated, and regulations must constitute the minimum practical to accommodate a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity

questions.answer: Amateur Service communications must be reasonably accommodated, and regulations must constitute the minimum practical to accommodate a legitimate purpose of the state or local entity

questions.question: What are the restrictions on the use of abbreviations or procedural signals in the amateur service?

choices.A: Only “Q” signals are permitted
choices.B: They may be used if they do not obscure the meaning of a message
choices.C: They are not permitted
choices.D: They are limited to those expressly listed in Part 97 of the FCC rules

questions.answer: They may be used if they do not obscure the meaning of a message

questions.question: When is it permissible to communicate with amateur stations in countries outside the areas administered by the Federal Communications Commission?

choices.A: Only when the foreign country has a formal third-party agreement filed with the FCC
choices.B: When the contact is with amateurs in any country except those whose administrations have notified the ITU that they object to such communications
choices.C: Only when the contact is with amateurs licensed by a country which is a member of the United Nations, or by a territory possessed by such a country
choices.D: Only when the contact is with amateurs licensed by a country which is a member of the International Amateur Radio Union, or by a territory possessed by such a country

questions.answer: When the contact is with amateurs in any country except those whose administrations have notified the ITU that they object to such communications

questions.question: On what HF frequencies are automatically controlled beacons permitted?

choices.A: On any frequency if power is less than 1 watt
choices.B: On any frequency if transmissions are in Morse code
choices.C: 21.08 MHz to 21.09 MHz

questions.answer: 28.20 MHz to 28.30 MHz

questions.question: What is the power limit for beacon stations?

choices.A: 10 watts PEP output
choices.B: 20 watts PEP output
choices.C: 100 watts PEP output

questions.answer: 100 watts PEP output

questions.question: Who or what determines “good engineering and good amateur practice,” as applied to the operation of an amateur station in all respects not covered by the Part 97 rules?

choices.A: The FCC
choices.B: The control operator
choices.C: The IEEE

questions.answer: The FCC

questions.question: Which of the following would disqualify a third party from participating in sending a message via an amateur station?

choices.A: The third party’s amateur license has been revoked and not reinstated
choices.B: The third party is not a US citizen
choices.C: The third party is speaking in a language other than English

questions.answer: The third party’s amateur license has been revoked and not reinstated

questions.question: When may a 10-meter repeater retransmit the 2-meter signal from a station that has a Technician class control operator?

choices.A: Under no circumstances
choices.B: Only if the station on 10-meters is operating under a Special Temporary Authorization allowing such retransmission
choices.C: Only during an FCC-declared general state of communications emergency
choices.D: Only if the 10-meter repeater control operator holds at least a General class license

questions.answer: Only if the 10-meter repeater control operator holds at least a General class license

questions.question: What is required to conduct communications with a digital station operating under automatic control outside the automatic control band segments?

choices.A: The station initiating the contact must be under local or remote control
choices.B: The interrogating transmission must be made by another automatically controlled station
choices.C: No third-party traffic may be transmitted
choices.D: The control operator of the interrogating station must hold an Amateur Extra class license

questions.answer: The station initiating the contact must be under local or remote control

questions.question: Which of the following conditions require a licensed amateur radio operator to take specific steps to avoid harmful interference to other users or facilities?

choices.A: When operating within one mile of an FCC Monitoring Station
choices.B: When using a band where the Amateur Service is secondary
choices.C: When a station is transmitting spread spectrum emissions

questions.answer: All these choices are correct

questions.question: What are the restrictions on messages sent to a third party in a country with which there is a Third-Party Agreement?

choices.A: They must relate to emergencies or disaster relief
choices.B: They must be for other licensed amateurs
choices.C: They must relate to amateur radio, or remarks of a personal character, or messages relating to emergencies or disaster relief
choices.D: The message must be limited to no longer than 1 minute in duration and the name of the third party must be recorded in the station log

questions.answer: They must relate to amateur radio, or remarks of a personal character, or messages relating to emergencies or disaster relief

questions.question: The frequency allocations of which ITU region apply to radio amateurs operating in North and South America?

choices.A: Region 4
choices.B: Region 3
choices.C: Region 2

questions.answer: Region 2

questions.question: In what part of the 2.4 GHz band may an amateur station communicate with non-licensed Wi-Fi stations?

choices.A: Anywhere in the band
choices.B: Channels 1 through 4
choices.C: Channels 42 through 45

questions.answer: No part

questions.question: What is the maximum PEP output allowed for spread spectrum transmissions?

choices.A: 100 milliwatts
choices.B: 10 watts
choices.C: 100 watts

questions.answer: 10 watts

questions.question: Why should an amateur operator normally avoid transmitting on 14.100, 18.110, 21.150, 24.930 and 28.200 MHz?

choices.A: A system of propagation beacon stations operates on those frequencies
choices.B: A system of automatic digital stations operates on those frequencies
choices.C: These frequencies are set aside for emergency operations
choices.D: These frequencies are set aside for bulletins from the FCC

questions.answer: A system of propagation beacon stations operates on those frequencies

questions.question: On what bands may automatically controlled stations transmitting RTTY or data emissions communicate with other automatically controlled digital stations?

choices.A: On any band segment where digital operation is permitted
choices.B: Anywhere in the non-phone segments of the 10-meter or shorter wavelength bands
choices.C: Only in the non-phone Extra Class segments of the bands
choices.D: Anywhere in the 6-meter or shorter wavelength bands, and in limited segments of some of the HF bands

questions.answer: Anywhere in the 6-meter or shorter wavelength bands, and in limited segments of some of the HF bands

questions.question: When may third-party messages be transmitted via remote control?

choices.A: Under any circumstances in which third party messages are permitted by FCC rules
choices.B: Under no circumstances except for emergencies
choices.C: Only when the message is intended for licensed radio amateurs
choices.D: Only when the message is intended for third parties in areas where licensing is controlled by the FCC

questions.answer: Under any circumstances in which third party messages are permitted by FCC rules
